summary: Snapcart survey (1,630 respondents, Feb–Mar 2026): 58% pick fresh scents such as citrus, green and aquatic; scent is the top purchase driver, ahead of price and brand.
angle: The 'fresh' pillar stays safe for high-volume SKUs.
idea: Keep a citrus-aquatic hero EDP in every launch wave; test a 'fresh after-shower' body mist extension.

summary: Local perfume founders expect gender-neutral green scents to gain ground throughout 2026.
angle: Candidate for a unisex variant.
idea: Launch a green-tea/fig-leaf unisex EDP named without gender cues.

summary: Consumers want scents that feel calming and safe; globally, fragrance is positioned as a tool for mood and wellbeing.
angle: Mood/ritual claims in product copy.
idea: Create a 'Calm' scent (lavender, chamomile, soft musk) with mood-led copy and a bedtime ritual card.

summary: Gourmands are moving beyond classic vanilla toward nutty, boozy, caramelised and creamy lactonic facets.
angle: Upgrade existing sweet variants.
source_name: OQEMA via Chemical UK, IDN Times
idea: Reformulate the sweetest variant toward toasted, nutty vanilla (hazelnut, caramel, tonka).

summary: Hyper-realistic fruit accords paired with matcha, espresso and hojicha inspirations.
angle: Fits a younger line or collaborations.
idea: Develop a 'Matcha Peach' or 'Hojicha Fig' EDP for a younger, café-culture line.

summary: Woods, musk and oud become softer and closer to the skin: quiet, understated luxury.
angle: Suits etiquette around scent in public spaces.
idea: Add a low-projection 'skin musk' EDP for office and public-transport wear.

summary: Saffron is named a hero note for 2026, with raspberry rising alongside fruity and gourmand trends.
angle: Differentiating note for a new EDP.
idea: Use saffron as the signature note in a new amber-woody EDP; raspberry as the fruity top.

summary: Notes of stone, pure water and cool air are rising as a fresh alternative that feels clean and restrained.
angle: Early signal; keep watching.
idea: Run a small panel test of a mineral/'rain on stone' accord before committing to a SKU.

summary: In men's fragrance, woody-fresh and clean masculine profiles are replacing sweet gourmands; unisex scents benefit too.
angle: Relevant for tropical-proof men's variants.
idea: Build a woody-fresh men's/unisex EDP tuned for heat and humidity (vetiver, cedar, citrus).

summary: Scarlett led Shopee in April 2026 (6.6% share) with EDP and Extrait under Rp60k, building a 'luxurious and long-lasting' perception.
angle: Price pressure in the high-concentration segment.
idea: Hold price below key competitors with an Extrait line; communicate longevity hours clearly.

summary: Layering (lotion, perfume, body mist, hair mist) is how people build a signature scent; body mists drive impulse purchases.
angle: Opportunity for layering bundles.
idea: Design layering bundles: EDP + matching body mist + hair mist with a layering guide.

summary: Fall report: fragrance is used to build atmosphere through candles, incense, home fragrance and layering rituals.
angle: Line extension into home scent.
idea: Extend the best-selling scent into a room spray or reed diffuser.

summary: On TikTok, perfume sells through narrative and 'vibe'; hooks like 'compliment monster' drive conversion. Viral cycle: ignition in 0–48 hours, conversion in 2–14 days.
angle: Have stock and content ready within 2 weeks of going viral.
idea: Prepare a 'compliment' storytelling content kit and safety stock for fast TikTok spikes.

summary: Viral TikTok perfume lists in 2026 are dominated by sweet gourmands and warm ambers; saffron-amber-woody comes up often.
angle: Compare with the local preference for fresh scents.
idea: Create a TikTok-friendly amber-vanilla hero, balanced with a fresh top for the tropics.

summary: Q2 2026: Mykonos 6.78%, Scarlett 5.46%, HMNS 5.09%; the top-5 order did not change from the previous quarter.
angle: Benchmark for SAFF's share.
idea: Benchmark SAFF's price, concentration and bottle size against the top 3 on Shopee.

summary: Ahmed Al Maghribi grew 128.76% in Q1 2026 vs Q4 2025 (then slipped in Q2, 1.35%); Afnan entered the top 10. The Fragrance Futures Index also notes Middle Eastern fragrance culture rising.
angle: Watch oud/Arabian styles in the mass segment.
idea: Test an accessible oud-amber or 'Arabian musk' variant for the mass segment.

summary: Mykonos is popular with Gen Alpha through heavy social media promotion and e-sports collaborations.
angle: IP/gaming collaborations as a lever.
idea: Explore a gaming or anime IP collaboration aimed at Gen Alpha/Gen Z.

summary: HMNS highlights soliflore (single-flower) perfumery from local materials, designed with international perfumers, for the mid segment.
angle: Local-ingredient stories are increasingly valued.
idea: Create a soliflore series from Indonesian flowers (melati, cempaka, sedap malam).

summary: 74.8% of online perfume buyers purchase from official stores for authenticity; Shopee (49.6%) narrowly leads Tokopedia (47.2%).
angle: Prioritise official stores on both platforms.
idea: Prioritise official-store exclusives and authenticity cues (seal, QR check) on packaging.

trend: Gen Z shops via Shopee & TikTok Shop
summary: Gen Z and upper-SES consumers are the most active in personal care; marketplaces matter more via Shopee and TikTok Shop, while perfume brand loyalty is highly fragmented.
angle: Low brand loyalty: regular innovation matters.
idea: Plan TikTok Shop-first launches with live-selling bundles for Gen Z.

summary: Local fragrance enthusiasts increasingly value experimental packaging and bottles as added value.
angle: Room for a signature bottle.
idea: Commission one signature collectible bottle shape for a hero line.

summary: Bright Gen Z designs are getting saturated; soft pastels, calming textures and soft-touch materials are rising.
angle: Visual refresh for the younger line.
idea: Refresh the younger line's packaging with soft pastels and a soft-touch matte coating.

summary: Packaging is now often seen first on a screen; differentiation concentrates where it drives conversion.
angle: Test designs at marketplace thumbnail size.
idea: Test every new pack at Shopee thumbnail size before final artwork.

summary: QR, NFC and RFID, mono-material formats and aluminium are expected to become more dominant.
angle: QR codes for notes storytelling.
idea: Add a QR on the box linking to notes, layering tips and an authenticity check.

summary: Paper-based packaging is moving into the mainstream; refill models remain but need reinvention.
angle: Early signal for the Indonesian market.
idea: Pilot a paper-based outer box or a refill pouch on one bestseller.

summary: With the emotional wellness trend, sensorial and playful packaging is used to create ritual moments.
angle: Unboxing as content.
idea: Design an unboxing moment (scented card, reveal layer) that works as content.

summary: Statista: 63.8% of global fragrance sales will come from non-luxury by end-2026; Indonesia is one of the markets to watch.
angle: Mass-premium remains the main growth space.
idea: Position new launches as mass-premium: Extrait quality at a mass price point.

summary: Several local brands are entering international markets by highlighting Indonesian character and raw materials.
angle: Nusantara ingredient stories.
idea: Build a 'Nusantara ingredients' story line with origin cards for export readiness.

summary: Korean fragrance brands are rising with clean, low-projection compositions that tell stories through heritage ingredients like perilla, Korean pine, makgeolli and hanji paper. Korean fragrance exports hit a record US$6.52M in January 2026.
angle: Local ingredient stories (pandan, rice, coffee) in a sheer Korean style.
idea: Create a sheer 'Nusantara' series around local heritage ingredients (pandan, rice, kopi).

summary: Rice and makgeolli perfumes with creamy-nutty facets are Korean bestsellers; at Esxence 2026, milky facets appeared in coffee, cocoa and matcha compositions.
angle: Rice/sticky-rice or coconut-milk accords as a local version.
idea: Develop a rice/sticky-rice milk or coconut-milk accord as a comforting milky scent.

summary: Kopi susu and aren (palm sugar) lattes remain the most sought-after drinks in Jakarta cafés, while a Korean brand launched a coffee perfume with Mane. Gourmands built on local drinks are still largely untapped.
angle: Turn Jakarta's best-selling drink into a perfume before competitors do.
idea: Launch a kopi susu gula aren gourmand EDP; partner with a Jakarta coffee chain.

summary: Tonka (CO2-extracted, creamy and almond-like) stood out in Esxence 2026 niche launches; the Fragrance Futures Index also lists tonka as an ingredient of interest.
angle: A more grown-up alternative to vanilla.
idea: Swap vanilla for tonka in a creamy almond-tonka gourmand.

summary: Clean accords (laundry, aldehydes, white musk) paired with Mediterranean green facets like lavender, fenugreek and immortelle at Esxence 2026.
angle: Bridge between the local 'fresh' preference and niche trends.
idea: Create a clean-laundry + herbal unisex scent (white musk, aldehydes, lavender).

summary: Fruit leads niche launches for Gen Z (peach, raspberry, kiwi); experts see realistic fig, guava and lychee rising while candy-like fruit fades.
angle: Local fruits (guava, lychee, mangosteen) done realistically, not candy-like.
idea: Launch realistic local fruits (jambu biji, leci, manggis) without candy sweetness.

summary: The Fragrance Futures Index 2026 lists alcohol-free and water-based formulations as a rising direction.
angle: Non-alcohol line; relevant for halal-minded and sensitive-skin consumers.
idea: Develop an alcohol-free, water-based mist or parfum; check halal certification path.

summary: Consumers build a 'fragrance wardrobe' for different moods and moments; 50 ml and discovery sets replace 100 ml as the default size.
angle: Cross-variant discovery set as an entry point.
idea: Create a 5×10 ml discovery wardrobe set across moods and occasions.

summary: Ingredient literacy is a rising behaviour: consumers want to know materials and their origins, not just note names.
angle: Copy that explains ingredients, not just mood.
idea: Add an ingredient-origin panel to packaging and PDP copy.

summary: Experts name lab-grown (biotech) naturals and AI-driven scent matching as the next innovations.
angle: Watch; could work as a scent quiz on e-commerce.
idea: Prototype an e-commerce scent-finder quiz; watch biotech naturals via suppliers.

summary: Korean brands combine fragrance, art and cafés in stores, plus DIY perfume festivals; in Indonesia, Blibli launched mood- and lifestyle-based fragrance curation.
angle: Booths/pop-ups with blending or layering activities.
idea: Run pop-ups with a blending/layering bar and a mood-based scent menu.

trend: Niche brands partner with big fragrance houses
summary: At Esxence 2026, independent brands increasingly collaborated with Givaudan and IFF, a sign the niche segment is professionalising.
angle: Access to new molecules through suppliers.
idea: Ask fragrance-house partners for access to their newest captives and accords.

summary: Candy-like gourmands and one-note 'cupcake' vanilla are seen as fading; overt sweetness is giving way to textured gourmands (toasted, creamy).
angle: Reduce sweetness when reformulating sweet variants.
idea: Audit sweet SKUs; cut overt sweetness or add texture (toasted, creamy) on reformulation.

summary: The single signature scent and 100 ml as the standard size are being left behind as the fragrance-wardrobe trend grows.
angle: Review the share of large-size SKUs.
idea: Shift new launches to 30–50 ml as the default; keep 100 ml only for proven bestsellers.

summary: Gendered labels are seen as fading; gender-neutral woody, leather and amber scents are rising.
angle: Name variants without gender.
idea: Name new variants by mood or material instead of 'pour homme/femme'.
